paragraphs: Overview. Jack in the Box Inc. (NASDAQ: JACK), a Delaware corporation (the "Company" or "Jack in the Box"), founded and headquartered in San Diego, California, is a restaurant company that operates and franchises Jack in the Box®, one of the nation's largest hamburger chains with 2,136 restaurants across 22 states, and Del Taco®, one of the nation's largest Mexican-American quick service restaurants ("QSR") chains with 576 restaurants across 18 states.
References to the Company throughout this Annual Report on Form 10-K are made using the first person notations of "we", "us" and "our."

In April, 2025, the Company announced a multi-faceted plan, which included exploring strategic alternatives for the Del Taco brand and the possible divestiture of that business. On October 15, 2025, the Company entered into a Stock Purchase Agreement (the "Purchase Agreement") with Yadav Enterprises, Inc., a California corporation ("Buyer") and Anil Yadav ("Buyer Guarantor") to sell to Buyer all of the issued and outstanding equity interests of Del Taco Holdings Inc., a Delaware corporation ("Del Taco"), which owns and operates the Company's Del Taco restaurant operations, for an aggregate purchase price of $115 million in cash, subject to certain closing cash, working capital, debt and transaction expense adjustments.

Jack in the Box. Jack in the Box restaurants offer a broad selection of distinctive products including classic burgers like its Jumbo Jack® and innovative product lines such as the Buttery Jack® and Smash Jack® burgers. Jack in the Box also offers quality products such as breakfast sandwiches with freshly cracked eggs, as well as craveable favorites such as tacos, curly fries, egg rolls, specialty sandwiches and real ice cream shakes, among many other items. Jack in the Box allows its guests to customize meals to their tastes and order any product on the menu when they want it, including breakfast at night, or burgers and chicken in the morning. The Jack in the Box trademark of variety and innovation has led to the development of five true day parts: breakfast, lunch, snack, dinner, and late night.

Jack in the Box opened its first restaurant in 1951 and has since become one of the nation's largest hamburger chains. Based on number of restaurants, the top 10 major markets of Jack in the Box comprise approximately 70% of the total system, and Jack in the Box is at least the fourth largest QSR hamburger chain in each of those major markets. As of September 28, 2025, Jack in the Box operated and franchised 2,136 quick-service restaurants, primarily in the western and southern United States, including two in Guam and three in Mexico. Of those total Jack in the Box restaurants at fiscal year-end, 1,986, or 93%, were franchised.

Del Taco. Del Taco offers a unique variety of both Mexican and American favorites such as burritos and fries, prepared fresh in every restaurant's kitchen with the value and convenience of a drive-thru. Del Taco's menu items taste better because they are made with quality ingredients like freshly grilled chicken and carne asada steak, fresh house-made guacamole, freshly grated cheddar cheese, slow-cooked beans made from scratch, and creamy Queso Blanco.

Founded in 1964, today Del Taco serves approximately two million guests each week at its restaurants. Del Taco's commitment to providing guests with the best quality and value for their money originates from cooking, chopping, shredding, and grilling menu items from scratch. As of September 28, 2025, Del Taco operated and franchised 576 restaurants. Of those total Del Taco restaurants at fiscal year-end, 444, or 77%, were franchised.

Our business strategies are rooted in our foundational principle of building a caring, high-performance culture that serves our franchisees and people well. We use this foundational principle as a guide while executing on our four strategic pillars:
•Strengthen Our Foundation by executing our "Jack on Track" plan, modernizing our technology, implementing a focused development strategy, and building strong relationships with our franchisees.

•Build Brand Loyalty by accelerating our reimage program, and executing our CRAVED marketing strategy, which includes our craveable menu items, value offerings, product innovation, and driving loyalty via our mobile app and web platforms.
•Drive Operations Excellence by evolving training efforts in our restaurants, execution of our brand standard systems, improving speed and consistency, and transforming the digital guest experience.
•Grow Restaurant Profits by capturing cost savings while driving sales and maintaining a strong guest experience.

This strategy builds on our historical strengths which include our uniquely broad menus, operational capabilities, passionate and loyal guests, committed team members and franchisees, and ability to invest in development and innovation that will deliver long term growth.

headings: Risks Related to Macroeconomic and Industry Conditions
Changes in the availability of and the cost of labor could adversely affect our business.
Changes in consumer confidence and declines in general economic conditions could negatively impact our financial results.
Increases in food and commodity costs could decrease our profit margins or result in a modified menu, which could adversely affect our financial results.
Failure to receive scheduled deliveries of high-quality food ingredients and other supplies could harm our operations and reputation.
Risks Related to Human Capital
Inability to attract, train and retain top-performing personnel could adversely impact our financial results or business.
Our business could be adversely affected by increased labor costs.
Unionization activities or labor disputes may disrupt our operations and affect our profitability.
Our insurance may not provide adequate levels of coverage against claims.
Risks Related to the Restaurant Industry
We face significant competition in the food service industry and our inability to compete may adversely affect our business.
Changes in demographic trends and in customer tastes and preferences could cause sales and the royalties that we receive from franchisees to decline.
Negative publicity relating to our business or industry could adversely impact our reputation.
We may not have the same resources as our competitors for marketing, advertising, and promotion.

We may be adversely impacted by severe weather conditions, natural disasters, terrorist acts, or civil unrest that could result in property damage, injury to employees and staff, and lost restaurant sales.
Risks Relating to Health and Safety
Food safety and food-borne illness concerns may have an adverse effect on our business by reducing demand and increasing costs.
Risks Related to Our Business Model and Strategy
We may not achieve our development goals.
Our highly-franchised business model presents a number of risks, and the failure of our franchisees to operate successful and profitable restaurants could negatively impact our business.
We are subject to financial and regulatory risks associated with our owned and leased properties and real estate development projects.
Risks Related to Legal and Regulatory Risks
Increasing regulatory and legal complexity may adversely affect restaurant operations and our financial results.

Governmental regulation, including in one or more of the following areas, may adversely affect our existing and future operations and results, including by harming our ability to profitably operate our restaurants.
The proliferation of federal, state, and local regulations increases our compliance risks, which in turn could adversely affect our business.
Legislation and regulations regarding our products and ingredients, including the nutritional content of our products, could impact customer preferences and negatively impact our financial results.
We may not be able to adequately protect our intellectual property, which could harm the value of our brands and adversely affect our business.
We are subject to increasing legal complexity and may be subject to claims or lawsuits that are costly to defend and could result in our payment of substantial damages or settlement costs.
Changes in tax laws, interpretations of existing tax law, or adverse determinations by tax authorities could adversely affect our income tax expense and income tax payments.
We may be subject to risk associated with disagreements with key stakeholders, such as franchisees.
Actions of activist stockholders could cause us to incur substantial costs, divert management's attention and resources, and have an adverse effect on our business.
Risks Related to Information and Technology
We are subject to the risk of cybersecurity breaches, intrusions, data loss, or other data security incidents.
Risks Related to Our Capital Structure
paragraphs: We caution you that our business and operations are subject to a number of risks and uncertainties. The factors listed below are important factors that could cause our actual results to differ materially from our historical results and from projections in the forward-looking statements contained in this report, in our other filings with the SEC, in our news releases, and in oral statements by our representatives. However, other factors that we do not anticipate or that we do not consider material based on currently available information may also have an adverse effect on our results.

Our business could be adversely impacted by increases in labor costs, including those increases triggered by regulatory actions regarding wages, scheduling and benefits; increased health care and workers' compensation insurance costs; increased wages and costs of other benefits necessary to attract and retain high quality employees with the right skill sets and increased wages, benefits and costs and inflationary and other pressure on wages now being experienced. The growth of our business can make it increasingly difficult to locate and hire sufficient numbers of employees, to maintain an effective system of internal controls, and to train employees to deliver a consistently high-quality product and customer experience, which could materially harm our business and results of operations.

The restaurant industry depends on consumer discretionary spending. We are impacted by consumer confidence, which is, in turn, influenced by general economic conditions and discretionary income levels. A material decline in consumer confidence or a decline in family "food away from home" spending could cause our financial results to decline. If economic conditions worsen, customer traffic could be adversely impacted if our customers choose to dine out less frequently or reduce the amount they spend on meals while dining out, which could cause our company and our franchised average restaurant sales to decline. An economic downturn may be caused by a variety of factors, such as macro-economic changes, increased unemployment rates, increased taxes, interest rates, or other changes in government fiscal policy. High gasoline prices, increased healthcare costs, declining home prices, and political unrest, foreign or domestic, may potentially contribute to an economic downturn, as may regional or local events, including natural disasters or local regulation. The impact of these factors may be exacerbated by the geographic profile of our brands. Specifically, approximately 70% of our systemwide restaurants are located in the states of California and Texas. Economic conditions, state and local laws, or government regulations affecting those states may therefore more greatly impact our results than would similar occurrences in other locations.

We and our franchisees are subject to volatility in food and commodity costs and availability. Accordingly, our profitability depends in part on our ability to anticipate and react to changes in food costs and availability. As is true of all companies in the restaurant industry, we are susceptible to increases in food costs that are outside of our control. Factors that can impact food and commodity costs include general economic conditions, inflation, labor shortages, seasonal fluctuations, weather and climate conditions, energy costs, global demand, trade protections and subsidies, food safety issues, infectious diseases, possible terrorist activity, cyberattacks, transportation issues, currency fluctuations, product recalls, and government regulatory schemes. Additionally, some of our produce, meats, and restaurant supplies are sourced from outside the United States. Any new or increased import duties, tariffs, or taxes, or other changes in U.S. trade or tax policy, could result in higher food and commodity costs that would adversely impact our financial results.

Weather and climate related issues, such as freezes or drought, may lead to temporary or even longer-term spikes in the prices of some ingredients such as produce and meats, or of livestock feed. Increasing weather volatility or other long-term changes in global weather patterns, including any changes associated with global climate change, could have a significant impact on the price or availability of some of our ingredients. Any increase in the prices of the ingredients most critical to our menu, such as beef, chicken, pork, tomatoes, lettuce, dairy products, and potatoes could adversely affect our financial results. In the event of cost increases with respect to one or more of our raw ingredients, we may choose to change our pricing or suspend serving a menu item rather than paying the increased cost for the particular ingredient.

We seek to manage food and commodity costs, including through extended fixed price contracts, strong category and commodity management, and purchasing fundamentals. However, certain commodities such as beef and pork do not lend themselves to fixed price contracts. We cannot assure you that we will successfully enter into fixed price contracts on a timely basis or on commercially favorable pricing terms. In addition, although our produce contracts contain predetermined price limits, we are subject to force majeure clauses resulting from weather or acts of God that may result in temporary spikes in costs.

paragraphs: For an understanding of the significant factors that influenced our performance during the fiscal year, we believe our Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations ("MD&A") should be read in conjunction with the consolidated financial statements and related notes included in this annual report as indexed on page F-1.
Comparisons under this heading refer to the 52-week periods ended September 28, 2025 and September 29, 2024, respectively. Our MD&A consists of the following sections:
•Overview — a general description of our business.
•Results of Operations — an analysis of our consolidated statements of earnings for fiscal 2025 compared to fiscal 2024.
•Liquidity and Capital Resources — an analysis of our cash flows, including capital expenditures, share repurchase activity, dividends, and known trends that may impact liquidity.
•Critical Accounting Estimates — a discussion of accounting policies that require critical judgments and estimates.
•New accounting pronouncements — a discussion of new accounting pronouncements, dates of implementation and the impact on our consolidated financial position or results of operations, if any.

We have included in our MD&A certain performance metrics that management uses to assess company performance and which we believe will be useful in analyzing and understanding our results of operations. These metrics include:

•Changes in sales at restaurants open more than one year ("same-store sales"), system restaurant sales, franchised restaurant sales, and average unit volumes ("AUVs"). Same-store sales, restaurant sales, and AUVs are presented for franchised restaurants. Franchise sales represent sales at franchise restaurants and are revenues of our franchisees. We do not record franchise sales as revenues; however, our royalty revenues and percentage rent revenues are calculated based on a percentage of franchise sales. We believe franchise and system same-store sales, franchised and system-wide sales, and AUV information are useful to investors as they have a direct effect on the Company's profitability.

Same-store sales, system restaurant sales, franchised restaurant sales and AUVs are not measurements determined in accordance with GAAP and should not be considered in isolation, or as an alternative to earnings from operations, or other similarly titled measures of other companies.

A comparison of our results of operations and cash flows for fiscal 2024 compared to fiscal 2023 can be found under Part II, "Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 29, 2024.

As of September 28, 2025 we operated and franchised 576 Del Taco restaurants across 18 states. We derive revenue from retail sales at company-operated restaurants and rental revenue, royalties (based upon a percent of sales), franchise fees and contributions for advertising and other services from franchisees.

paragraphs: 概述。Jack in the Box Inc. (NASDAQ: JACK)，一家設立於德克薩斯州的公司（本公司或「Jack in the Box」），成立並總部設於美國加州聖地牙哥，是一家餐廳公司，經營與特許經營Jack in the Box®，為美國最大的漢堡連鎖餐廳之一，擁有2,136家餐廳，分佈於22個州，以及Del Taco®，為美國最大的墨西哥裔快速服務餐廳（QSR）連鎖之一，擁有576家餐廳，分佈於18個州。
本年度報告10-K文件中提及本公司時，均使用第一人稱的「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」。

2025年4月，本公司宣佈了一項多面向的計畫，其中包括探討Del Taco品牌的戰略選擇，以及該業務可能出售的可能。2025年10月15日，本公司與Yadav Enterprises, Inc.，一家加州公司（買方）及Anil Yadav（買方擔保人）簽訂股票購買協議（購買協議），以現金總計115 百萬美元出售Del Taco Holdings Inc.，一家設立於德克薩斯州的公司（Del Taco）的所有已發行及現存的股權，該公司擁有並經營本公司Del Taco餐廳業務，交易價格為115 百萬美元現金，扣除特定的關閉現金、營運資金、負債及交易費用調整後。

Jack in the Box。Jack in the Box餐廳提供廣泛的獨特產品選擇，包括經典漢堡如其Jumbo Jack®，以及創新產品線如Buttery Jack®和Smash Jack®漢堡。Jack in the Box也提供高品質產品，如以新鮮敲碎蛋製作的早餐三明治，以及令人難忘的美食如墨西哥捲餅、捲餅薯條、蛋餅、特製三明治及真實冰淇淋聖代，以及其他許多商品。Jack in the Box讓顧客可以根據個人口味自訂餐點，並在想要的時間點點任何產品，包括晚上喫早餐，或早上喫漢堡和雞肉。Jack in the Box的多樣性與創新品牌已發展出五種真正的用餐時段：早餐、午餐、點心、晚餐及深夜。

Jack in the Box於1951年開設第一家餐廳，並成為美國最大的漢堡連鎖之一。根據餐廳數量，Jack in the Box前十大市場約佔總體系統的70%，且在這些主要市場中，Jack in the Box至少為第四大QSR漢堡連鎖。截至2025年9月28日，Jack in the Box經營與特許經營2,136家快速服務餐廳，主要位於美國西部與南部，包括 Guam 兩家與墨西哥三家。在會計年度結算日，總計2,136家Jack in the Box餐廳中，1,986家，或93%，為特許經營。
Del Taco。Del Taco提供獨特的墨西哥與美國美食選擇，如墨西哥捲餅與薯條，並在每家餐廳的廚房中現做現賣，並提供便利的 drive-thru 服務。Del Taco的餐點更美味，因為使用高品質的食材，如新鮮烤製的雞肉與carne asada 牛排、現做現喫的店內製造的guacamole、新鮮磨碎的cheddar奶酪、慢煮的豆子與濃鬱的Queso Blanco乳酪。
Del Taco於1964年成立，目前每天約服務兩百萬位顧客。Del Taco對提供顧客最佳品質與價值的承諾，源自於從頭開始製作、切碎、撕碎與烤製餐點。截至2025年9月28日，Del Taco經營與特許經營576家餐廳。在會計年度結算日，總計576家Del Taco餐廳中，444家，或77%，為特許經營。
我們的業務策略根植於我們的基礎原則，即建立一個關懷、高績效的文化，以服務特許經營者與員工。我們使用這個基礎原則作為指引，執行我們的四大戰略支柱：
•透過執行我們的 "Jack on Track" 計畫，現代化我們的科技，實施聚焦的發展策略，並與我們的加盟者建立強固的關係，來強化我們的基礎。
•透過加速我們的 reimage 計畫，並執行我們的 CRAVED 營銷策略，來建立品牌忠誠度，此策略包含我們的 craveable 菜單項目、價值提案、產品創新，以及透過我們的行動應用程式和網路平台來推動忠誠度。
•透過進化我們餐廳的培訓努力，執行我們的品牌標準系統，改善速度與一致性，並轉變數位顧客體驗，來推動運營卓越。
•透過捕捉成本節省，同時推動銷售並維持強勁的顧客體驗，來增加餐廳利潤。
此策略建立在我們的歷史優勢之上，包括我們獨特廣泛的菜單、運營能力、熱情且忠誠的顧客、投入的團隊成員與加盟者，以及投資於開發與創新以實現長期成長的能力。

paragraphs: 為瞭解影響我們在會計年度表現的重大因素，我們認為應配合本年度財務報告中所附的合併財務報表及相關附註，一併閱讀我們的管理層討論與分析（"MD&A"）部分，如索引頁 F-1 所列。
本節比較資料係指截至 2025 年 9 月 28 日及 2024 年 9 月 29 日之 52 週期間的比較。我們的 MD&A 包含以下各節：
•總覽 — 有關我們業務的一般性描述。
•營運成果 — 有關我們合併損益表於 2025 會計年度與 2024 會計年度之比較分析。
•流動性及資本資源 — 有關我們現金流量之分析，包括資本支出、股票回購活動、股息及可能影響流動性的已知趨勢。
•關鍵會計估計 — 有關需運用關鍵判斷與估計之會計政策之討論。
•新會計準則 — 有關新會計準則之討論，包括實施日期及對我們合併財務狀況或營運成果之影響（如有）。
我們已在 MD&A 中包含若干管理層用以評估公司表現之績效指標，我們認為這些指標對分析與理解我們營運成果將有助益。這些指標包括：

• 餐廳營業額變動（指營運超過一年的餐廳營業額（"同店營業額"）、系統餐廳營業額、特許經營餐廳營業額，以及平均單店營業額（"AUVs"））。同店營業額、餐廳營業額及AUVs為特許經營餐廳所呈現的資料。特許經營營業額代表特許經營餐廳的營業額，並為我們特許經營者的收入。我們並未將特許經營營業額列為收入；然而，我們的特許經營費用收入及百分比租金收入是根據特許經營營業額的百分比計算。我們認為特許經營及系統同店營業額、特許經營及系統營業額，以及AUV資訊對投資人而言是有用的，因為這些資訊對本公司獲利有直接影響。
同店營業額、系統餐廳營業額、特許經營餐廳營業額及AUVs並非根據GAAP所定義的衡量指標，不應孤立地或作為營運獲利或其他公司類似名稱指標的替代指標來考量。
本公司財務狀況及營運成果在財務年度2024年與財務年度2023年的比較，可見於年度報告書第II部，"第7項 管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析"，於財務年度2024年9月29日結業的10-K表格年報中。

Jack in the Box Inc.（"本公司"）於1951年成立，經營及特許經營Jack in the Box®與Del Taco®速食餐廳。截至2025年9月28日，本公司經營及特許經營2,136間Jack in the Box餐廳，主要位於美國西部與南部，包括墨西哥3間與關島2間。截至2025年9月28日，本公司經營及特許經營18個州的576間Del Taco餐廳。本公司收入來自公司自營餐廳的零售營業額，以及來自特許經營者的租金收入、特許經營費用（根據銷售額百分比計算）、特許經營費及廣告與其他服務的費用。

2025年4月23日，本公司宣佈了一項多面向計畫，包括探討Del Taco品牌的戰略選擇，以及可能出售該業務。2025年10月15日，本公司與Yadav Enterprises, Inc.（位於加州的公司）（"買方"）及Anil Yadav（"買方擔保人"）簽訂股票買賣協議（"買賣協議"），以現金總計115百萬美元出售Del Taco Holdings Inc.（位於德拉瓦州的公司）（"Del Taco"）所有已發行且現存的股權，該公司擁有並營運本公司Del Taco餐廳業務，並根據交易關閉時的現金、營運資金、負債及交易費用調整後的淨現金進行計算。

headings: 與總體經濟及產業條件相關的風險
勞動力的可得性與成本的變動可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
消費者信心的變動及總體經濟條件的惡化可能對本公司的財務結果產生負面影響。
食品及原物料成本的增加可能降低本公司的毛利率或導致菜單調整，此情形可能對本公司的財務結果產生負面影響。
未能如期收到高品質食品原料及其他供應品可能影響本公司營運及聲譽。
與人力資本相關的風險
無法吸引、培訓及留住表現優秀的員工可能對本公司的財務結果或業務產生負面影響。
勞動成本的增加可能對本公司業務產生負面影響。
工會化活動或勞資爭議可能幹擾我們的營運並影響我們的獲利能力。
我們的保險可能無法提供足夠的保障範圍以應對賠償聲請。
與餐飲業相關的風險
我們在餐飲服務業面臨激烈的競爭，若無法有效競爭，可能對我們的業務造成不利影響。
人口結構趨勢的變化以及顧客口味與偏好的改變，可能導致銷售額及我們從加盟者那裡收到的特許經營權費用下降。
與我們的業務或產業相關的負面宣傳可能對我們的聲譽造成不利影響。
我們可能沒有與競爭對手同等的資源用於行銷、廣告與宣傳。
我們可能因嚴重天氣條件、自然災害、恐怖攻擊或民變等事件而受到不利影響，這些事件可能導致財產損壞、員工與工作人員受傷，以及餐飲銷售額減少。
與健康與安全相關的風險
食品安全及食源性疾病之關注可能對本公司業務產生負面影響，導致需求減少且成本增加。
與本公司商業模式及策略相關的風險
本公司可能無法達成其發展目標。
本公司高度特許經營的商業模式面臨許多風險，若特許經營者無法經營成功且獲利之餐廳，將對本公司業務產生負面影響。
本公司受自有及租賃不動產及不動產開發專案之財務及法規風險影響。
與法律及法規相關的風險
法規及法律複雜性增加可能對餐廳營運及本公司財務結果產生負面影響。
政府規範，包括在一個或多個以下領域，可能不利於我們現有及未來的營運與結果，包括透過影響我們以獲利方式經營餐廳的能力。
聯邦、州及地方規範的增加，會提高我們的合規風險，進而可能不利於我們的業務。
關於我們產品及原料的立法與規範，包括我們產品的營養成分，可能影響顧客偏好，並對我們的財務結果造成負面影響。
我們可能無法充分保護我們的智慧財產權，這可能會損害我們品牌的價值，並對我們的業務造成不利影響。
我們面臨日益增加的法律複雜性，並可能面臨成本高昂的聲請或訴訟，且可能導致我們需支付重大賠償或和解費用。
稅法的變更、現有稅法的解釋，或稅務機關不利的裁定，可能對我們的所得稅費用及所得稅繳納造成不利影響。
我們可能面臨與關鍵股東之間意見不合所產生的風險，例如特許經營權持有人。
活躍股東的行動可能導致我們產生重大成本，分散管理階層的注意力與資源，並對我們的業務產生不利影響。
資訊與科技相關風險
本公司面臨資訊科技相關風險，包括網路安全事件、入侵、資料遺失或其他資料安全事故的風險。
本公司資本結構相關風險
paragraphs: 我們提醒您，我們的業務與運作面臨許多風險與不確定性。下列列出的因素是重要的因素，可能導致我們的實際結果與歷史結果或本報告、其他向美國證券交易委員會（SEC）提交的文件、新聞發佈會以及我們代表的口頭陳述中所包含的預測性陳述有重大差異。然而，我們可能未預見或未視其為重要因素，基於目前可取得的資訊，這些因素也可能對我們的結果產生不利影響。
我們的業務可能因勞動成本增加而受到負面影響，包括因規範行動而導致的工資、排班與福利成本增加；醫療保險與員工補償保險成本增加；吸引並留住具備正確技能的高素質員工所需的工資與其他福利成本增加，以及因通貨膨脹或其他因素導致的工資壓力增加。我們業務的成長可能使我們更難尋找並僱用足夠的員工、維持有效的內部控制系統，以及培訓員工以提供一致的高品質產品與顧客體驗，這可能會對我們的業務與營運結果造成重大損害。

餐飲業依賴消費者可自由支配支出。我們受到消費者信心的影響，而消費者信心又受到總體經濟狀況與可自由支配收入水平的影響。消費者信心大幅下降或家庭「外食」支出減少，可能會導致我們的財務結果下降。如果經濟狀況惡化，若我們的顧客減少外食頻率或減少在外用餐時的開支，可能會對我們的客流量造成負面影響，進而導致我們的公司與特許經營平均餐廳銷售額下降。經濟衰退可能由多種因素引起，例如總體經濟變動、失業率上升、稅率提高、利率或政府財政政策的其他變動。高汽油價格、醫療費用增加、住宅價格下跌以及國內或國際的政治動盪，可能促成經濟衰退，區域性或地方性事件，包括天然災害或地方規範，也可能導致經濟衰退。這些因素的影響可能因我們品牌在地理分佈上的特性而更加嚴重。具體而言，約70%的我們系統內餐廳位於加利福尼亞州與德克薩斯州。因此，這些州的經濟狀況、州或地方法律，或影響這些州的政府規範，可能比其他地區的類似情況對我們的結果產生更顯著的影響。

我們與我們的特許經營商會受到食品與原物料成本與供應的波動影響。因此，我們的獲利在一定程度上取決於我們預測並應對食品成本與供應變動的能力。如同所有餐飲業公司一樣，我們會受到無法控制的食品成本上升的影響。影響食品與原物料成本的因素包括總體經濟狀況、通貨膨脹、勞動力短缺、季節性波動、天氣與氣候條件、能源成本、全球需求、貿易保護與補貼、食品安全問題、傳染病、可能的恐怖活動、網路攻擊、運輸問題、貨幣波動、產品回收以及政府規範方案。此外，我們部分的農產品、肉類與餐飲供應來自美國境外。任何新的或增加的進口關稅、稅收或其他美國貿易或稅收政策的變動，都可能導致食品與原物料成本上升，進而對我們的財務結果產生不利影響。

天氣與氣候相關問題，例如凍結或乾旱，可能導致某些原料如農產品與肉類，或牲畜飼料的價格出現暫時或更長時間的上漲。氣候變動或全球氣候變遷所導致的氣候模式變動增加，或任何與全球氣候變遷相關的變化，可能對我們部分原料的價格或供應產生重大影響。任何與我們餐點息息相關的關鍵原料價格上漲，例如牛肉、雞肉、豬肉、番茄、生菜、乳製品與馬鈴薯，都可能對我們的財務結果產生不利影響。若我們的原料成本因某種或某些原料而增加，我們可能選擇調整價格或暫停供應某項餐點，而不是承擔該原料的增加成本。
我們致力於管理食品與原物料成本，包括透過延長固定價格契約、強化類別與原物料管理以及採購基本原則。然而，某些原物料如牛肉與豬肉並不適合透過固定價格契約來管理。我們無法保證我們會在合適的時間或商業上有利的價格條件下成功簽訂固定價格契約。此外，雖然我們的農產品契約包含預先確定的價格上限，我們仍會受到因天氣或天災等不可抗力條款所導致的暫時性成本上漲的影響。
